```dafny
method sort_array(array: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires array != null
    ensures result != null
    ensures |result| == |array|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |array| ==> result[i] == array[i] || result[i] == array[i] // Ensure that the result is a copy of the array
    ensures (array.Length == 0 ==> result == [])
    ensures (array.Length == 1 ==> result == array)
    ensures (sum(array[0], array[array.Length - 1]) % 2 == 1 ==> sorted(result, true)) // result is sorted in ascending order if sum is odd
    ensures (sum(array[0], array[array.Length - 1]) % 2 == 0 ==> sorted(result, false)) // result is sorted in descending order if sum is even

    // Helper method to check if a sequence is sorted
    method sorted(seq: seq<int>, ascending: bool) returns (isSorted: bool)
        requires seq != null
        requires |seq| > 0
        ensures isSorted ==> forall i :: 0 <= i < |seq| - 1 ==> (ascending ==> seq[i] <= seq[i + 1] || !ascending ==> seq[i] >= seq[i + 1])
```

def sort_array(array):
    """
    Given an array of non-negative integers, return a copy of the given array after sorting,
    you will sort the given array in ascending order if the sum( first index value, last index value) is odd,
    or sort it in descending order if the sum( first index value, last index value) is even.

    Note:
    * don't change the given array.

    Examples:
    * sort_array([]) => []
    * sort_array([5]) => [5]
    * sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5]) => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    * sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5, 6]) => [6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
    """
problem_data.canonical_solution: return [] if len(array) == 0 else sorted(array, reverse= (array[0]+array[-1]) % 2 == 0)
